name: unslop
cost: Free (CC BY 4.0, credit required). Image generation through a paid service is optional and asks first
short: A skill that audits an AI-looking UI for slop, sets a design direction and fixes the screen pass by pass.
what: It looks for the usual signs of vibecoded UI: purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy and uneven spacing. Then it sets a direction from your product and works through spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion, in that order. It works with Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML and CSS, and on a live site when all you have is a link. It can also make a short square video of the screen changing.
who: Anyone whose app, dashboard or landing page looks AI-made and who wants it to look designed. If your screen already looks good, it says so and suggests small tweaks instead of a redesign.
needs: For the story video: Playwright and ffmpeg
Optional: an image service like fal, Replicate, OpenAI images or Higgsfield, for hero images

steps.title: Copy the skill into your skills folder
steps.text: For a single project, copy it into `.claude/skills/` inside that project instead.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/

steps.title: Run it on a screen
steps.text: Type `/unslop` with what you want, or just ask in your own words. It audits the screen and proposes a direction before it edits anything, so you can steer it early.

try.label: From the README
try.text: `/unslop my landing page and make the story video so I can post it`. Or try it first on the two vibecoded screens in the repo's examples folder.

watch: If no image service is connected, it offers to connect one as an MCP server. It shows the prompt and asks before every paid generation.
It edits your UI code, so work on a branch or commit first.
